g: (informal, predicative only) Of mediocre quality; unremarkable.
(Caribbean, chiefly Trinidad and Tobago) Used to negate the following verb; (am/are/is/do/does) not.

(informal, chiefly Canada, Upper Midwestern US, New Zealand, Australia, UK, Ireland, South Africa, India, Hong Kong, Singapore, Commonwealth) Used as a tag question, to emphasise what goes before or to request that the listener express an opinion about what has been said.
These hot dogs are pretty good, eh?
In isolation, a request for repetition or clarification of what has just been said.
—I've been studying Graphiurus murinus. —Eh? Studying what?
In isolation, expressing surprise or confusion.
—You're going to be a dad! —Eh? You're joking!
(chiefly Canada) An interjection used to ascertain the continued attention of someone addressed by the speaker.
I went to the restaurant, eh, but my friends didn't show up.
Expressing apathy or lack of enthusiasm; meh.
A First Nations government on the West Coast of Vancouver Island in British Columbia, Canada.
The four Hebrew letters that can serve as vowels: alef, he, vav, and yodh.
(medicine, pathology) Any of a group of inherited connective tissue disorders caused by a defect in the synthesis of collagen, and resulting in abnormally elastic skin, joints, muscles, etc.
Of or relating to Christian Gottfried Ehrenberg (1795–1876), German naturalist, zoologist, comparative anatomist, geologist, and microscopist.
Of or relating to Andrew S. C. Ehrenberg (1926–2010), English statistician and marketing scientist.
Any of a group of equations that describe changes in specific heat capacity and derivatives of specific volume in second-order phase transitions.
(thermodynamics) A model of diffusion used to explain the second law of thermodynamics, considering a number of particles in two containers, which independently change container at a certain rate.
Of or relating to Paul Ehrenfest (1880–1933), Austrian physicist and mathematician.
An optical illusion in which the sides of a square placed inside a pattern of concentric circles take an apparent curved shape.
(botany) Belonging to the family Ehretiaceae in order Boraginales.
Any grass of the subfamily Ehrhartoideae (now known as Oryzoideae)
(mineralogy) A triclinic-pinacoidal mineral containing beryllium, calcium, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and zinc.
A reagent made from paradimethylaminobenzaldehyde, ethanol and concentrated hydrochloric acid, primarily used to identify indoles.
The presence of Ehrlichia bacteria in the bloodstream.
Relating to, or afflicted with, ehrlichemia.
(medicine) A tick-borne disease caused by infection with bacteria of the genus Ehrlichia.
Cyperus laevigatus, a species of sedge.
